subject: Culture
title: Graduation Origins
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Graduation Origins.

hook.text: The graduation cap and gown come from medieval monks. Universities started in monasteries.

buildup.text: The cap—mortarboard—represents the scholar's authority. The gown marks separation from the common crowd.

discovery.text: Throwing the cap started at the US Naval Academy in 1912, when graduates no longer needed their midshipman hats.

twist.text: In many countries, graduation isn't celebrated. German students finish quietly. The American ceremony is the outlier.

climax.text: Graduation works as ritual because it's public. The community witnesses the transformation.

punchline.text: The hat flies because the old self is gone.

quiz.question: Where did the tradition of throwing graduation caps originate?
